en.title: Hideo Kojima Wants to Die Before a Movie Starts, Not During
en.summary: Legendary game designer Hideo Kojima has revealed his peculiar ideal end-of-life scenario: passing away in a movie theater just as a film is about to begin. This reflects his profound love for cinema and the unique anticipation of a cinematic experience.
en.body:
Hideo Kojima, the visionary behind the **Metal Gear Solid** and **Death Stranding** series, has shared a deeply personal and somewhat unconventional wish for his final moments: to pass away in a movie theater, precisely as a film is about to commence.

Speaking at a film festival in Rome, the 62-year-old game director, a self-proclaimed cinephile who famously states that 70% of his body is made of movies, elaborated on this peculiar desire. He finds the moments *before* a film begins to be the most potent – the dimming lights, the swell of trailers, and the palpable anticipation of the narrative about to unfold. It's this specific slice of cinematic time, pregnant with possibility and just before the main event, where he envisions his own end.

> “I’ve always thought that when I die, I would like to die in a movie theater. I love the bit before the movie starts the most. Enter the movie theater, the lights go off and commercials and trailers play, yeah? I’d like to die just before the movie starts.” — Hideo Kojima

This isn't the first time Kojima has contemplated his mortality and legacy. In the past, he’s spoken about leaving behind a USB stick filled with game ideas for his staff to develop after his passing. This recent declaration, delivered with a characteristic blend of seriousness and a knowing smile, underscores his unique perspective on life, death, and the art forms that have shaped him. The pandemic profoundly impacted his outlook, as he revealed a serious illness and an eye operation made him confront his own aging and creative limitations more directly than turning 60.

## A Creator's Enduring Drive

For fans who follow Kojima's every move, these reflections are more than just morbid curiosities; they are windows into the soul of an artist who lives and breathes his craft. His desire to die while *making* something, as he’s stated in other interviews, is a testament to his unwavering dedication. This sentiment resonates deeply with a fanbase that eagerly awaits his next project, understanding that his creative drive is intrinsically linked to his very existence. The thought of him being unable to create, especially after his health scare, adds a layer of urgency and poignancy to his public statements.

## What's Next for Kojima Productions

While Kojima contemplates his final curtain call, his studio, Kojima Productions, remains active. As of 2026, he is still deeply involved in game development, with fans eagerly anticipating future projects that are sure to push the boundaries of interactive storytelling, much like his previous acclaimed works. Details on his next game are scarce, but his continued passion ensures that whatever comes next will carry his distinctive auteur signature.

content_raw: Veteran game director and self-confessed movie buff Hideo Kojima revealed that he’d like to pass away in a movie theater, just as the film itself is about to start. The 62-year-old made the comment at a film festival in Rome earlier this month, and recently shared a clip of the moment on his official X account . “I’ve always thought that when I die, I would like to die in a movie theater,” Kojima said in Japanese, as translated by IGN. He goes on to explain that “I love the bit before the movie starts the most. Enter the movie theater, the lights go off and commercials and trailers play, yeah? I’d like to die just before the movie starts.” Kojima delivered this declaration in a serious tone but with a hint of a smile. The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator is, after all, a prolific cinemaphile, proclaiming on his X account profile that 70% of his body is made up of movies. This isn't the first time Kojima has spoken about his own death. Last year, hot on the heels of revealing a number of discarded video game ideas and even an idea for a ‘Forgetting Game’ where the main character gradually forgets important information and abilities if you take too long a break from playing, Kojima said he had left his staff a USB stick of game ideas for after he dies . As reported by VGC , Kojima issued the morbid revelation to Edge magazine , and discussed his change of thinking that occurred during the pandemic. “Turning 60 was less of a turning point in my life than my experiences during the pandemic,” he said. “I fell seriously ill at that time, and also had an eye operation. Until then, I didn’t think I was old, you know? I just didn’t feel my age, and I assumed I would be able to create for as long as I live. “But then I became sick, and I couldn’t create anything. And I saw lots of people around me passing away at that time. I was confronted with death. Of course, I recovered, but now I was thinking, ‘Wait, how many years do I have left to make a game or a film?’ Perhaps I have 10 years?” Also last year, Kojima discussed his fears as he has got older. "What I am most afraid of is time," he told GQ . "I am afraid of dying and having dementia. I am afraid of forgetting things when I get old. I am afraid that I won't even realise what I am forgetting." Kojima made this latest quip at the Piccolo America Foundation’s 12th edition of Il Cinema in Piazza, an outdoor film festival in Rome. As reported by Game Surf , he took part in panel discussions and introduced several movies. On July 4, he introduced Shunya Ito’s 1972 film Female Prisoner Scorpion: Jailhouse 41, the second movie in Japanese studio Toei’s exploitation series. The movie and its star, Meiko Kaji, were a big influence on Quentin Tarantino, so much so that Tarantino borrowed Urami Bushi (the theme song sung by Kaji) for the soundtrack to Kill Bill.
